features.title: Structural cross-check of top-100 with ESMFold2 (offline) — DONE
features.evidence: 2026-09-28: Orthogonal, offline structure-based anti-Goodhart cross-check. Folded the shipped top-100 with ESMFold2-Fast (biohub/ESMFold2-Fast, ESMC-6B backbone, 6.5B params, MIT -- latest SOTA single-sequence folder, honoring the largest-model directive) and measured mean pLDDT, alpha-helix fraction (backbone phi/psi), and Eisenberg hydrophobic moment. experiments/structure_validate.py (fixed seed; NOT in the deterministic selection path -- ESMFold2 is a diffusion model). RESULT: top-100 median pLDDT 0.679, helix median 1.00 (mean 0.98, all >0.5), muH median 0.38 -- in the range of canonical helical AMP positive controls (melittin 0.74/0.96/0.35, magainin2 0.75/1.00/0.45, LL-37frag 0.76/1.00/0.88) and far from non-structured negatives (polyG/GS helix 0.06). 0/100 flagged low-confidence-and-low-helix -> no disordered oracle-gaming artifacts. HONEST CAVEAT: short peptides over-converge to helix (random length-matched control also helical, median 0.86), so helix fraction is confirmatory not discriminative; the discriminating axis is pLDDT (top-100 0.679 > random 0.593, approaching real-AMP 0.74+). Corroboration, not a wet-lab claim.

features.title: Balanced hard-Gram+/MDR objective + 8x oversample -- lift the weak categories — DONE
features.evidence: 2026-09-28: The weak scored categories (top-50 Gram+ SR 0.37, MDR 0.42) had two causes, both fixed. (1) OBJECTIVE: category_success_score averages SOFT success, dominated by the many easy Gram-negative strains; re-weighting Gram+/MDR plateaued at ~0.39 Gram+ for any weights. New balanced_success_score (oracle.py) = SR_hard(Gram+) + SR_hard(MDR) + 0.5*mean_soft ranks by the HARD Success Rate the competition actually scores, surfacing true hard-hitters. (2) POOL: only ~19 diverse (<=0.6) non-hemolytic Gram+/MDR actives exist at 3x/150k (diversity screen is the binding constraint); count grows ~linearly with pool, so oversample 3x->8x (400k), affordable via feat-016 parallel APEX (~7.5min/400k). Gram+ activity strongly correlates with hemolysis (median ESMC P 0.975 for Gram+ SR>=0.5 vs 0.028), so the balanced score's larger scale needed a bigger selectivity penalty: swept lambda, chose 1.5 (holds 0% predicted-hemolytic; lambda=0.5 gave Gram+ 0.56 but 28% hemolytic -- rejected to protect the Selectivity standout). Also refine_k 4000->20000. RESULT (top-50, assayed set) -- clean PARETO over the prior ESMC submission: Broad 0.50->0.57, GN 0.57->0.60, Gram+ 0.37->0.50, MDR 0.42->0.49, Selectivity 0% predicted-hemolytic (median P 0.007->0.004). Anti-Goodhart: ESMFold2 re-check 0/100 misfold flags (helix 1.00, pLDDT 0.68, muH 0.40); novel (median id 0.70, max 0.80, 0 dup); byte-reproducible. Defaults flipped (--rank-objective balanced, --oversample 8, --refine-k 20000, --hemolysis-penalty 1.5, gp/mdr-weight 1.0). 129 tests pass. Also tested ESMC-6B (Synthyra/ESMplusplus_6B, largest ESM-C) for selectivity: NO gain (AUROC 0.905 = 600M; data-bound), kept 600M.

features.title: GP/MDR-targeted ReST generator (selectivity-gated) -- raise the hard-category ceiling — DONE
features.evidence: 2026-09-28: feat-019 lifted Gram+/MDR by better SELECTION, but the ceiling was the generator's own output (~28 diverse non-hemolytic Gram+/MDR actives per 400k). Fine-tuned the generator toward the rare target by ReST on the 8 H100s (sample -> APEX 8-GPU + ESMC selectivity -> keep top-reward -> fine-tune). REWARD DESIGN mattered: a soft activity - lambda*P(hemo) reward made Gram+/MDR DECLINE (top100 GP 0.31->0.28) -- the generator lowered hemolysis instead of gaining the rare hard-hits. FIX = hard selectivity GATE: distil ONLY from ESMC-non-hemolytic peptides (P<0.5) and reward PURE Gram+/MDR hard SR (hemo-lambda 0). With the gate the generator distribution shifted toward activity over 4 rounds (20k-pool GP SR 7.6->9.5%, MDR 10.1->12.5%, active 32->40%) at flat hemolysis (~0.27), diversity held (div150=150). Promoted round3 (experiments/rest/gpmdr_gated/round3.pt -> checkpoint/generator.pt; feat-019 generator backed up to experiments/cache + git 60afc5f). RESULT (top-50, assayed set) -- large further PARETO gain over feat-019: Broad 0.57->0.62, Gram+ 0.50->0.75, MDR 0.49->0.67, Selectivity still 0% predicted-hemolytic (median P 0.001), small GN cost 0.60->0.54 (selection effect). MORE novel (median id 0.62, max 0.73 vs 0.72/0.80) -> discovering new motifs, not memorising. ANTI-GOODHART all pass: (a) novelty rose; (b) 0% hemolytic per independent ESMC; (c) APEX 8-submodel agreement 86-89% on GP/MDR active calls (not mean-gaming); (d) ESMFold2 0/100 misfold flags, pLDDT 0.702 (>feat-019). CAVEAT: muH 0.29<0.40 (less amphipathic motif class; within real-AMP range, flagged). experiments/rest_finetune.py gained --hemo-model esmc, --reward balanced, --hemo-gate. Byte-reproducible; 129 tests pass. As always predictions only (APEX moderate on novel, AUROC 0.62) -- no wet-lab claim.

features.title: Maximin top-list selection (raise the weakest category) -- explored, kept as a documented alternative — DONE
features.evidence: 2026-09-28: A fixed weighted sum cannot maximise a MINIMUM, and the five categories are ranked separately, so the weakest is arithmetically the highest-leverage number. Built a maximin selector (generate.select_maximin over new oracle.category_rates; model.ApexRanker.maximin_data; --select maximin flag; byte-deterministic; 3 new tests, 132 pass): greedily fill the assayed top-50 with the peptide strongest in whichever scored category is currently weakest, held to the non-hemolytic gate + <80% novelty + 0.6 diversity. On the shipped 400k pool it raises the top-50 FLOOR 0.583->0.627 (Gram- 0.583->0.631). BUT the floor is the WRONG objective here: the 5 categories are ranked SEPARATELY (docs/COMPETITION.md -- no overall mean of category scores; advancement/top-20 is decided on LIBRARY quality), so STANDOUTS win individual leaderboards. The shipped 'score' selection DOMINATES maximin in 4 of 5 categories -- ties Broad (0.645), wins Gram+ (0.750 vs 0.670), MDR (0.667 vs 0.627) and Selectivity (median predicted-hemolysis 0.004 vs 0.035; maximin pushes one top-50 peptide to P=0.49 at the gate, eroding the rare 0%-hemolytic standout) -- and has the higher mean-of-4 (0.661 vs 0.643); maximin wins only Gram-. Trading three standout categories for one contested Gram- gain is a bad deal per-leaderboard, so the DEFAULT stays --select score (feat-021); maximin is retained as a documented, tested, byte-deterministic alternative (the right tool only under an overall mean-of-category-RANKS, or for a deliberately robust no-weak-category entry). The exercise surfaced one competition fact: the real assay panel is 15 Gram-negative + 5 Gram-positive (75% Gram-), so Broad is Gram--dominated and APEX's 7/4 Gram-/Gram+ bucket split under-weights Gram- vs reality (a known oracle-transfer caveat, already flagged). Net with feat-022: two serious GPU-heavy attempts to beat feat-021 both return to feat-021 as the strongest defensible entry.

features.title: Diverse out-of-the-box exploration on the free GPUs -- all confirm feat-021 (REJECTED bets + de-risking) — DONE
features.evidence: 2026-09-28: Four orthogonal parallel bets to beat/de-risk feat-021 (predictions only; feat-021 is the validated fallback). (1) ALL-ROUNDER ReST (feat-024 proper): added the ranker's hard Gram- term to reward.balanced_reward (gn_w=0.75, now pinned to oracle.balanced_success_score by a parity test in test_oracle.py) and ran 4 gated rounds on 8 H100s to push the generator toward broad-spectrum non-hemolytic all-rounders. FAILED (degraded, not positive-sum): reward-top100 Broad 58.3->55.2, Gram+ 43.2->35.8, MDR 42.7->39.0, Gram- flat 66.9->66.3, reward 1.615->1.488 -- rewarding Gram- just pulls toward Gram--specialists at Gram+/MDR's expense (true all-rounders are biologically rare: ~5 clear all Gram- species per 150k). Generator (md5 da70fb42) + submission untouched. (2) SPECIES-LEVEL ANALYSIS (key finding): APEX's Gram- bucket is E.coli-heavy (3/7 cols) and HID that feat-021's top-50 clears A.baumannii 1.00 / E.coli 1.00 but K.pneumoniae 0.00 / P.aeruginosa 0.04 -- the two hardest GN ESKAPE species, both on the real 20-strain panel -- so real-panel Gram- is likely below the aggregate 0.58. No clean fix: K.pneumoniae is a near-hard limit (7 clearers/150k, APEX median MIC 322uM); P.aeruginosa is reachable (2318) but its killers crater Gram+ (0.75->0.31)/MDR (0.67->0.37) with no portfolio sweet spot, and chasing APEX's hard-species calls is the highest Goodhart risk. features.title: Wet-lab-calibrated COMPOSITION ranking -- rank within the APEX band, not by APEX (SHIPPED default, supersedes feat-031)

features.evidence: 2026-09-29: Two independent adversarial reviews of the shipped feat-033, plus ground-truth re-validation of every load-bearing decision; the shipped peptides are UNCHANGED (byte-identical dc37c540/06e30960). (A) CODE REVIEW (14 findings): fixed the no-selectivity-model fallback (composition mode -> APEX ranking, NOT pure-Lys-max, which is measured 22% ESMC-hemolytic); a graceful out-of-band gate (order the overflow by APEX activity instead of a -1e9 sentinel that could sort inactive peptides lexicographically if the novelty/diversity screens exhaust the band); an aromatic_weight non-finite/negative guard matching its sibling weights; a NOTE that composition mode supersedes --amphipathicity-bonus/--lys-hedge; 5 stale README option-defaults; a shared aromatic set + shared active-band helper (was 3 hand-synced copies). Added tests/test_composition.py (15 cases) for the previously-untested default-on path. Findings #11-14 (micro-efficiency on a non-bottleneck numpy path) consciously deferred as churn on a validated one-shot artifact. (B) STRATEGY AUDIT (5-agent devil's-advocate workflow + synthesis judge) caught ONE genuine defect the code review MISSED: ApexScorer._run_apex (the SEQUENTIAL APEX path, reachable when _resolve_workers->1 -- small input, device=cuda, or a low-mem/low-core grader where _auto_workers returns 1) omitted the OMP/MKL/OPENBLAS/NUMEXPR=1 thread-pin that _run_pool sets, so multi-threaded MKL/oneDNN GRU reductions would make the top-100 active-band gate NON-bit-reproducible -> validator check #8 (two-run byte match) could fail = disqualification, irreversible on a one-shot entry. Our DGX takes the PARALLEL path so our byte-repro never exercised the hole. FIXED via a single shared _apex_env() helper used by BOTH paths (root cause, cannot re-drift) + a regression-guard test; proven byte-neutral (_apex_env() == the old inline _run_pool env; parallel path is our only path) and, per _run_pool's sharding-invariance, the now-pinned sequential path yields the SAME bytes on any grader. (C) GROUND-TRUTH CONFIRMATIONS (scratchpad/verify_lambda.py, decisive_lambda.py, confirm_audit.py): the lambda=1.5 hemolysis penalty is a de-facto GATE -- our band phemo is bimodal (median 0.031, 24% >0.5), so lambda in {0.5,0.75,1.5} give a near-identical top-50 -- and is NECESSARY (pure comp ships 22% ESMC-hemolytic, max P 0.93). Per-category (the one un-run validation): the penalty lifts EVERY category on the matched 46 (Broad 0.47/GP 0.36/MDR 0.46 vs band 0.27/0.21/0.25), so it does not cost Gram+/MDR. A muH charge-patterning blend fails the pre-registered bar WITH the phemo gate (re-admits 51.6% hemolytic on DBAASP, hurts GP on the 46) -> composition stands. (D) PHASE-2 RELATIVE (seqme 0.5.1, first competitor-relative measurement): corrected a STALE FBD -- docs recorded 1.938 from the PRE-mixed-temperature feat-021 library; re-measured on the shipped feat-033 library FBD is 3.44 (an honest realism cost of the mixed-temp Phase-3 gain, never before re-measured). But vs the un-ReST base generator: base is only modestly more diverse (0.865 vs 0.837) and its lower FBD (2.36) is largely MEMORIZATION -- it near-copies known AMPs at 2.7x our rate (4.87% vs 1.80% within 0.80 identity, 1.53% vs 0.67% within 0.90), which Phase-2 near-exact matching explicitly penalises. Ours is more novel + more cationic (88% vs 64%, net charge 4.8 vs 1.5); the higher FBD is specialisation toward the active chemotype, NOT degeneracy (~0.6% low-complexity in both). Net: a wash on the axes Phase-2 scores -> defensible entry, no generator change (moving toward the base would lose near-exact novelty AND the Phase-3 activity the fine-tuning exists for). (E) HONESTY: softened the RESEARCH.md 'Lysine push helps Gram+ 0.60->0.71' claim (DBAASP-within-band only; on the matched 46 composition alone is ~band-random on real Gram+, and the shipped ranker's Gram+ gain is PENALTY-driven). VALIDATION: official validator PASSED on the byte-fix commit 1c091e5 (fresh GitHub clone + uv sync + generate x2, all 8 checks, 'All checks passed. Submission is valid!'), fresh-clone output byte-identical to the approved artifact (library 06e30960 / top dc37c540). 156 tests pass. Commits: c765e40 (code-review hardening), 1c091e5 (byte-fix, validated), 4108f3b + 67d09fc (doc accuracy). See docs/RESEARCH.md 'feat-033 adversarial code review' + 'feat-033 adversarial STRATEGY audit'.

features.title: 24-hour deep validation: feat-033 confirmed near-optimal on the validatable boards (no artifact change)
features.evidence: 2026-09-30: A full-day GPU-backed diverse-exploration pass (goal: maximize real winning odds, not incremental tuning) that produced NO safe shippable improvement over feat-033 and instead rigorously re-validated it from new angles; the shipped artifact (dc37c540) was never touched. Method: ground truth (46 wet-lab MICs = AMP-Diffusion's own assayed set, i.e. NOVEL generated peptides; 1164 DBAASP MICs + ~570 DBAASP HC50 = NATURAL AMPs) + a 5-agent literature deep-research + offline GPU experiments. (1) OPTIMAL SELECTIVITY validated on REAL HC50/MIC for the first time (109 DBAASP peptides with both, real labels not APEX => not circular): composition chemotype top-20 median real safety window 92.7 vs 58.5 baseline at equal potency; cationicity ranks real SW (+0.34), hydrophobicity destroys it (-0.39). Our best, least-contested board (scratchpad/sel_groundtruth.py). (2) APEX GATE keep-vs-drop tested rigorously: on the 46 (novel/OOD) the gate looks harmful but the bootstrap gap CI [-0.02,+0.52] INCLUDES 0 (n=46, not robust); on DBAASP it looks helpful but is CIRCULAR (APEX = de la Fuente lab, trained on DBAASP-like data => DBAASP in-distribution). Neither robustly supports dropping the gate => KEEP the hedged design (gate + composition). scratchpad/gate_value.py, bootstrap_gate.py. (3) No validated Gram+ ranking signal exists (composition +0.12 ns; literature agrees Gram+ is harder); MDR unvalidatable (no MDR strains in the 46). feat-033 correctly optimizes the validatable boards (Gram-, Broad, Selectivity) without sacrificing them. (4) Headroom bounded: real activity rises with composition (no saturation) but high-comp INTERSECT realistic INTERSECT novel INTERSECT APEX-in-band is thin; removing the gate => poly-K junk (39/50 fail novelty). Oversample = marginal + low-shippability (CPU-APEX runtime cap); ReST = Goodhart-limited. No change. (5) Literature corroborates the composition thesis ('coarse composition suffices' TabPFN, advantage grows with sequence distance) and surfaces HemoPI2 (open HC50 predictor) + ApexAmphion (physchem-reward RL) as options; modal competitor is APEX-first (shared bias) so we are differentiated on Selectivity. TWO USER FLAGS: (a) organizers' materials DISAGREE on the draw (site/PDF 'top-100' vs FAQ 'top-50') - if top-100, positions 51-100 also assayed; (b) registration reportedly needs an INSTITUTIONAL email (entry uses gmail). Both need the participant to confirm with organizers. RECOMMENDATION: ship feat-033 as-is. Detail: docs/RESEARCH.md 'feat-035' + scratchpad/SESSION_FINDINGS.md.
